Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the SIG grid. We can and do support tenant-scoped preservation for a narrow set of telemetry and inference artifacts; the answer depends on the artifact class (request payloads, KV cache, prefix cache, debug traces, structured audit logs). Short summary here:

- Ephemeral inference payloads: default TTL 30 days; can be extended for legal hold snapshots.
- KV/prefix cache: normally transient (minutes-hours) and not persisted to durable logs except when debug-mode or forensics-enabled; we can configure persistent snapshots on a per-tenant basis.
- Structured audit logs (API auth, routing, billing): retained 365 days by default.

We’ll put together a small evidence bundle + an internal runbook for legal hold steps. Marissa will pull the artifacts and produce a PDF you can hand to auditors. Jonas, can the runtime team confirm snapshot verification (hashing + time-based proofs) and give a short screenshot of the KV TTL UI?

Quick technical clarification:

- When we say "snapshot" we create an immutable object in our customer escrow bucket with metadata: tenant_id, snapshot_time, artifact_types included, and a SHA256 manifest. The snapshot is writable only by the retention service and immutable thereafter.
- For prefix/KV caches: the runtime can be configured to persist caches to ephemeral blob storage for forensics; those blobs follow the same legal-hold path as snapshots.
- Index correlation: we create an index file that maps request IDs -> trace IDs to make exports auditable. That index itself is treated as metadata and is retained for the same window as the snapshot.

Attaching a quick screenshot of the KV TTL panel for illustration (kv-ttl-screenshot.png). If Hemera prefers cryptographic receipts (e.g., signed timestamped manifests), we can also provide an HSM-signed attestation next business day (requires a signed NDA if they want private-key proofs crossed with PII-preserving samples).
